section: the maths of parallel sampling
text: Three selectors, three formulas. pass@k: the ceiling a perfect verifier reaches If one sample solves a problem with probability p, and samples are independent: pass@ k = 1 − ( 1 − p ) k p the single-sample success probability on this problem k the number of samples drawn (1 − p) k the probability that all k fail With p = 0.2: one sample succeeds 20% of the time; five give 1 − 0.8 5 = 1 − 0.32768 = 0.672; ten give 1 − 0.8 10 = 1 − 0.107 = 0.893.
